title: acre draws figures of computed data without a generator script
body:
Two figures of the nail sequence aligner were drawn in acre at `c846b14`. `pipeline.acre` shows the whole `nail search` pipeline. `cloud.acre` explains how libnail's cloud search fills its DP matrix one anti-diagonal at a time, and how the profile HMM's states map onto the arrays that hold their scores. Both sit in nail's `tmp-claude/2026-11-13-acre-pipeline/`, which git ignores, beside the scripts that made them.

Neither file was written by hand. Each started as a hand-written template, `pipeline.acre.in` or `cloud.acre.in`, with placeholders such as `@FWD@`. A Python script, `gen.py` or `gen_cloud.py`, read a program's output and replaced each placeholder with generated `line`, `box` and `text` nodes. The generated files run to about 2,000 lines. Most of those lines are one of three things:

| what the figure shows | how the script drew it | nodes |
|---|---|---|
| a region of the DP matrix: a cloud, the row bounds | one thick `line` per anti-diagonal, or one `box` per matrix row | 278 to 526 per region |
| the alignment path through the matrix | one `line` per step | 327 |
| a zoomed grid of DP cells, 12 by 13 | one `box` per cell, one `text` per heading | 181 per grid, 5 grids |

Each child of this issue is one feature that would have let the template be the figure, or one behaviour that cost a render to find. They are separate because each can land, or be rejected, without the others.
